We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need to output JSON tree: root molecule, children reactions etc.

We need to select appropriate templates for each step: likely step1: amide formation (reverse of coupling) -> break amide bond between C(=O) and N of anilide (Nc3ccccc3N). So precursors: carboxylic acid (the unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The unsaturated acid is derived from Doebner modification: reverse of that gives aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. So step2: break C=C and carboxyl to give aldehyde and malonic acid. The aldehyde is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group? Actually the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl sulfonyl group via aromatic ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)N...)cc2 attached to sulfonyl group. So the aldehyde precursor would be aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl group attached: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl group is attached to the aromatic ring via S(=O)(=O) attached to N of first phenyl (para to methyl). Actually target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So we have two phenyl rings: ring A (with methyl) bearing sulfonamide linking to sulfonyl attached to ring B. Ring B has the unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step1: amide formation reverse: break amide to give unsaturated acid (alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid) attached to ring B, and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step2: Doebner reverse: break unsaturated acid to give aromatic aldehyde (with sulfonyl attached) and malonic acid. Step3: sulfonamide formation reverse: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and amine (the aniline of ring A). But we have sulfonamide linking ring A amine to sulfonyl attached to ring B. So reverse: break N-S bond to give amine (ring A) and sulfonyl chloride attached to ring B (i.e., aromatic sulfonyl chloride). That seems plausible.

We need template IDs. We don't know IDs; we can search. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each step.

First step: amide formation (forward) is coupling of carboxylic acid and amine. So reverse we need template that breaks C-N amide bond, forming carboxylic acid and amine. Use criteria: functional_groups_broken: "carboxylic acid"? Actually forward breaks carboxylic acid (C-O) and forms amide. So reverse break amide. Let's search for templates with bonds broken: "C-N". But we need template ID. Let's search with criteria: bonds_broken maybe "C-N". Use tool.
